subject: Post-call: open-model parity & eval next steps
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Claire Huang <claire@atlasai.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@atlasai.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: open-model parity & eval next steps

Hi Claire / Tom,

Thanks again for the call this morning — appreciate the clarity on the end-user tolerance for hallucination and the production latency constraints ("95th < 600ms when batched"). High-level recap and proposed next steps below so we have something concrete to align on.

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary goal: replace the current proprietary scoring model for intent classification + short-form generation while keeping equal-or-better precision.
- Acceptance criteria (you mentioned): macro-F1 >= 0.78 on the curated testset; Hallucination rate <= 2% on the generative QA set.
- Cost target: <= 40% of current per-call infra spend, or equivalent ROI measured over the first 100k calls.

Our recommended eval plan (short):
1) Side-by-side blind eval across three variants:
   - Atlas baseline (your current proprietary model)
   - Open model candidate: Llama-2-13B-instruct (standard fp16)
   - Redwood candidate: Redwood-3b-quant (4-bit), tuned prompt/template set
2) Use your production-like promptset (attached as rdw_eval_promptset_v2.csv) + 1k held-out labelled examples for metric calculations.
3) We will run automated benchmarks that capture: macro-F1, generation hallucination (heuristic + human spot-check), latency distribution (p50/p95) under the target batching profile. Link to our runner: https://redwood.ai/evals/RDW-3741-parity-report

Key questions for you
- Confirm the held-out labels: can you share the 1k labels (or allow a read-only S3 link)?
- Is the 2% hallucination threshold strict (hard pass/fail) or advisory?

Proposed next steps / timeline
- Tue 2026-03-17 10:00–11:00 PT: kickoff (we'll demo the eval harness and share runbook)
- 48-hour blind run (we'll mask system tags so your reviewers don’t know which model produced each output)
- Presentation of parity report + suggested rollout path the following week.

Attachments: rdw_eval_promptset_v2.csv (prompt variants and templating rules), parity_summary.xlsx (placeholder summary sheet), benchmark-run-0315.log (sample run).

If that timeline works I’ll send a calendar invite and a short NDA addendum for the dataset access.

Best,
Rafael
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
r.mendes@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0194

From: Claire Huang <claire@atlasai.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: open-model parity & eval next steps

Thanks Rafael — this looks good and very thorough. A couple quick clarifications: 

1) Labels: we can provision a read-only S3 bucket for the 1k held-out examples by EOD Monday. Is that enough for you or do you need different access?
2) Hallucination threshold: the 2% is a hard bar for us for prod rollout on generative QA items. For classification we can be a bit more flexible if precision stays high.
3) For the side-by-side: can you confirm whether the Llama-2 run will be identical infra (same GPU type) as the Redwood candidate? We want the comparison to be as apples-to-apples as possible.

Also — is there any PII handling we need to worry about for the promptset? We scrubbed names but there are some user excerpts that could be considered sensitive.

—Claire
Head of ML Operations, AtlasAI
claire@atlasai.com

On Sun, Mar 15, 2026 at 09:12 AM Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com> wrote:
> (quoted message omitted for brevity)
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Claire Huang <claire@atlasai.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 13:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: open-model parity & eval next steps

Raf — quick notes from product/ops perspective: 

- Infra parity: we can run both Llama-2-13B and Redwood-3b-quant on the same A100/80GB reservation so latency comparisons are direct; we’ll bake in identical batch sizes for fairness. Call the config: A100-1x, batch_size=8, seq_len=512.
- PII: request that Atlas accept our standard Data Access Addendum (short form). We’ll also run an automated PII detection pass on inbound promptset and redact if needed; any redaction will be logged and available to you.
- Eval design: add an adversarial slice of 200 examples designed to probe hallucination (we can build that overnight). For acceptance: suggest adding a regression alert — if a candidate model drops below baseline F1 by >0.03 on any major class, the run is flagged and we stop the rollout.
- Logging: we can share anonymized token-level logs and deterministic seeds; full raw logs require the DAA.

I’ll coordinate with infra to reserve capacity for Tue/Wed. If Claire confirms S3 access, we’ll seed the runner Monday night.

—Lauren
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Claire Huang <claire@atlasai.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@atlasai.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 14:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: open-model parity & eval next steps

Claire — excellent, thanks for the quick answers and the S3 offer. We’ll proceed as follows once you confirm the bucket link: 

1) I’ll send a calendar invite for Tue 2026-03-17 10:00 PT for kickoff.
2) Lauren’s team will reserve A100 capacity and seed the runner with rdw_eval_promptset_v2.csv + the adversarial slice.
3) We’ll run a blind 48-hour job and produce the parity report (link will be shared).
4) If Atlas requires, we can run an extra variant: Llama-2-13B quantized (to 4-bit) to explore cost/latency trade-offs — that’s optional but recommended if cost parity is tight.

DocuSign / legal: I will attach the short DAA and a one-page SOW for the eval (no charge for the 48-hour benchmark). Expect those in a separate email.

One more ask: do you have a preferred acceptance authorizer for final sign-off (name + title)? We’ll include them in the parity report delivery meeting.

Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff.
Rafael
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
r.mendes@redwood.com
